leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene with the same three names (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) and a citation built on the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated insulating and superconducting states, with the superconducting mechanism deliberately left out of the wording. They share the view that this is the cleanest theory-to-experiment chain on the shortlist, and all of them concede that the pairing mechanism is unsettled, that Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto have an earlier moire band-structure claim, and that Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby and others sit outside the credit. They differ in how much weight these concessions carry: Mehlig and Eriksson say a Nobel discovery does not need a settled mechanism, while Danielsson and Olsson name maturity as the main reason a committee might wait. Mehlig and Eriksson name B049 or B026 as the fallback if a stricter maturity bar is set.

Three members prefer optical lattice clocks with a two-person credit (Katori and Ye). They share the view that the credit divides cleanly into Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's demonstration of 10^-18 performance, that independent confirmation over about two decades is strong, and that the citation should be written around the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice so it does not read as a third prize in the comb and ion-control lineage. They also share the reservations that the fundamental-physics results so far are null tests, that the redefinition of the second has not happened, and that Lemonde, Ludlow and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups have arguable claims. Lindroth and Kroll judge the atomic-structure arguments from inside the field, and Pearce changed to this position from B026 after reading the opening statements.

One member prefers ultracold-atom quantum simulation in optical lattices with Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, having moved off circuit QED (B040) after colleagues raised the 2025 circuit prize and the omission of Girvin and Devoret. The case rests on a clear discovery chain (Jaksch-Zoller proposal, Mott transition, quantum gas microscopy) and two decades of replication. The same member names the weaknesses: Cirac is left out of a four-name list, Jaksch is not credited, Haensch, Esslinger and Bakr have arguable claims, the topic sits near the 2001 and 2012 prizes, and the analogue-simulation payoff has not been demonstrated. B012 appears as a first alternative for Olsson and a second alternative for Kroll and Lindroth, but no one else prefers it.

areas_of_agreement: All eight round-1 configurations are single-part prizes; the committee has not yet split into two-part configurations, and Danielsson explicitly sees no combination that keeps the union within three people.
B009, B049 and B012 are the three candidates that carry preferred-configuration support, and B009 and B049 are named as alternatives by members across the split.

Most members treat B009 as scientifically strong with an unusually clean prediction-then-observation chain, and treat B049 as the more mature, more cleanly attributed candidate; the disagreement is about how to trade these, not about the quality of either.

Four members (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Pearce) now regard circuit QED (B040) as hard to lead with because of the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits and the omission of Girvin and Devoret; Johansson has withdrawn it from his preferred configuration.

B011 (active matter) has no supporter beyond its proposer; Johansson, Kroll, Danielsson, Eriksson and Pearce all cite Yuhai Tu's omission from the credit and limited quantitative tests of the Toner-Tu exponents.

B023 (Higgs, ATLAS and CMS) is not in any other member's preferred configuration; Kroll, Johansson, Olsson and Mehlig responded that crediting three project leaders for collaborations of thousands is hard to square with the individual-laureate standard.

The B026 trio (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is recognised as conceptually important and mature, but members who discussed it, including its own opening proponent, say the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (with Zhang deceased) and of the 3D topological-insulator contributors makes allocation harder than for B009.

Several members agree that any citation should be worded around the established findings, the flat bands and observed states for B009 and the magic-wavelength lattice for B049, rather than around unsettled mechanisms or applications.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks (B049) are a discovery or a decisive improvement in measurement: Danielsson, Johansson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson stress the precision-measurement character and null fundamental tests, while Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce stress the new many-atom magic-wavelength regime, the millimetre-scale redshift measurements and the concrete route to redefining the second.

Whether B009 opens a new class of quantum matter that outweighs a refinement of measurement, as Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson argue, or whether its interpretation is too open to weigh against a mature and fully understood error budget, as Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce argue.

Whether the committee should weigh specialist technical judgement or breadth of opening support: Lindroth acknowledges her own bias toward atomic structure, Kroll ranked B009 last because it is outside his specialty, and Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson point to B009 being ranked by all eight members and placed in the top three by five.

Whether quantum simulation with ultracold atoms (B012) is an established physics result (Mott transition, imaging of correlations) or a capability whose promised payoff over classical simulation is not delivered; Eriksson ranked it seventh on this ground and Johansson ranked it first.

Whether active-matter hydrodynamics (B011) has an experimental anchor equivalent to the confirming discoveries behind B009 or B049; Mehlig asks the others to consider colloidal-roller and vibrated-rod experiments, but no other member has said these settle the exponents.
attribution_disputes: B009: whether Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto weaken the Bistritzer-MacDonald theory credit (Mehlig and Eriksson say the quantitative magic-angle condition is the decisive prediction), and whether the experimental credit belongs to Jarillo-Herrero alone or should extend to Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby and others within a three-person limit.

B049: whether Lemonde, Ludlow or the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups have a claim strong enough to require a third name; Kroll and Lindroth say a two-name award is defensible if the omission is stated openly, and Pearce flags that the record-accuracy figures supplied have not been independently checked.

B012: four names are supplied for three places; Mehlig alone proposes Cirac in place of Greiner, Johansson argues for Zoller on the grounds that the Jaksch-Zoller proposal is what the experiments implemented, and Jaksch, Haensch, Esslinger and Bakr are outside the credit.

B026: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe realisation that triggered the experiment, Zhang is deceased, and the 3D contributors (Fu, Kane, Moore, Hasan and others) are a separate chapter; Pearce would return to B026 only if a fair framing around the quantum spin Hall effect can be found.

B040 and B011: Girvin and Devoret are outside the circuit-QED credit, and Yuhai Tu is outside the active-matter credit, so those three-person configurations are each missing a figure other members regard as central.
maturity_disputes: B009 is about eight years from the key experiments, with the pairing mechanism, the phase diagram and twist-angle and sample disorder still debated. Eriksson and Mehlig argue a discovery does not need a settled mechanism, whereas Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Pearce say the prize gains from waiting, and Olsson notes that disorder and strain are part of what must be understood before the correlated phases are attributed.

B049 has about two decades of independent confirmation, but the redefinition of the second has not happened: Lindroth says waiting would reward administrative timing instead of the discovery, whereas Pearce lists waiting for the redefinition as an open uncertainty and Danielsson says a mature metrology result can wait.

B012 is mature in replication but its analogue-simulation advantage over classical methods is not yet shown, and Johansson asks whether B009 will overtake it as the pairing mechanism becomes better understood.
B040 is mature in science but close in time to the 2025 circuit prize, which several members treat as a timing problem rather than a scientific one.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (B040): works in circuit and waveguide QED and leads WACQT at Chalmers, has Chalmers colleagues (Delsing, Wilson) and a frequent co-author (Frisk Kockum) in that community, and says he would recuse himself from a final decision on B040 or weigh his views accordingly; B040 is no longer in his preferred configuration.

Kroll (B049): spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, linked to the JILA environment of Jun Ye, with no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye; he asks the committee to decide whether this requires recusal on B049. Kroll also notes overlap of his European quantum-memory collaborations with the Cirac and Zoller community (B012) and involvement in WACQT (B040).

Pearce (chair): would flag professional proximity and consider recusal if B047 (IceCube neutrinos, Halzen) were seriously considered, given PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+ and XL-Calibur work; no conflict is apparent for B049, B026 or B009. B047 is not in any preferred configuration.
Olsson and Johansson: both are at Chalmers, which Olsson describes as a collegial connection that matters only if B040 becomes a deciding candidate.

Lindroth (B049) and Mehlig (B011) disclose disciplinary closeness to the field, not a personal tie, and note it as possible bias; Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson report no specific conflict for the leading candidates.
questions_for_round2: Is B009 or B049 the committee's lead configuration, and if the committee wants a single prize this year, what would have to be established about the unresolved pairing mechanism for B009, or about distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes for B049, for the other camp to accept it?

For B009, does the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction stand as the decisive theory contribution against the earlier moire work of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, and which experimental contribution (Jarillo-Herrero's group or the parallel hBN-encapsulation work of Dean and others) is to be credited within three names?

For B049, is a two-name award of Katori and Ye defensible against Lemonde, Ludlow and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups, and can a citation centred on the magic-wavelength lattice be drafted that is clearly distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize? Which specific accuracy and stability results should the committee verify first?

Should the committee wait for the formal redefinition of the second before recognising B049, and does a comparable wait apply to B009 for the pairing mechanism? Is an equal standard of maturity being applied to the two?

If B012 is to be considered, who is the right theory name among Zoller, Cirac and Jaksch, should the experimental credit be Bloch and Greiner, and does the citation avoid overlap with the 2001 and 2012 prizes?
Can B026 be framed around the quantum spin Hall effect so that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 3D topological-insulator work are handled honestly, or does it remain a deferred candidate?

Do Johansson and Kroll want B040 considered this year given the 2025 prize, the omission of Girvin and Devoret and the disclosed connections, and does Kroll's Hall connection require any change in how B049 is handled?

Can any member who ranks B011 or B023 high identify an experimental anchor (for B011) or an allocation principle for three individuals within a large collaboration (for B023) that would put either into the same discussion as B009 and B049?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files divide four, three and one among B009, B049 and B012, and the members who prefer one of the first two name the other as an alternative. Disagreement is less about scientific quality than about maturity, novelty relative to earlier prizes, and how many credited names each candidate leaves out. Only positions stated in the eight files are counted; the chair's own preference for B049 is one of the three on that side and is not given extra weight.
